1 Kor 15,24b-26 Βασιλείαν ὧδε λέγει τοὺς βασιλευομένους, ἤτοι τὴν ἰδίαν σάρκα ἣν
βελτιῶσαι ὁ υἱὸς παρέδωκε τῷ πατρί, οὐκέτι βασιλευομένην ὡς δούλου μορφὴν ἀλλ' ὡς οὖσαν σάρκα τοῦ λόγου ὃ ἔστιν αὐτοῦ τοῦ υἱοῦ, ἀναδείξας τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ μορφὴν ἐν αὐτῇ. τότε γὰρ ἀπειληφότος τοῦ υἱοῦ τὴν δόξαν ἣν εἶχε πρὸ τοῦ τὸν κόσμον εἶναι, ὡς ὑφ' ἑνὸς βασιλέως πατρὸς καὶ υἱοῦ βασιλευθήσονται. δεῖ οὖν τὸν Χριστὸν βασιλεύειν ὑπὲρ τῆς ὅλων προκοπῆς ἕως οὗ πάντες οἱ διὰ τὸ ἁμαρτάνειν ἐχθροὶ ὑπὸ πόδας αὐτοῦ τιθῶσιν, καταλύοντος αὐτοῦ πᾶσαν τυραννικὴν ἐξουσίαν, μεθ' ἣν καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ ἀρχίκακος καταλύεται θάνατος, ἐπείπερ πᾶσα ἑνουμένη αὐτῷ ψυχὴ ὑφισταμένη θάνατον τὸν ἑνούμενον τῇ κακίᾳ. 1 Kor 15,27-28 Πρός τε τὴν Ἑλλήνων μυθολογίαν τε καὶ ἀπάτην εἰρῆσθαι ταῦτα εἰπόντες τῶν φασκόντων πατραλοίας εἶναι θεούς, καὶ ὅτι τῆς ἐκκλησίας ὑποτασσομένης αὐτὸς λέγεται ὑποτάττεσθαι, οἰκειούμενος τῆς ἐκκλησίας τοὺς διωγμοὺς καὶ τὰ πάθη καὶ τὴν ὑποταγήν. 1 Kor 15,29 Οἱ ἀπὸ Μαρκίωνος ἀντὶ ἀφωτίστων τεθνεώτων βαπτίζουσι ζῶντας, οὐκ εἰδότες ὅτι τὸ βάπτισμα σώζει μόνον τὸν εἰληφότα αὐτό. ὁ δὲ ἀπόστολος νεκροὺς λέγει τὰ σώματα ὑπὲρ ὧν βαπτιζόμεθα· τῷ γὰρ ἰδίῳ λόγῳ ἄνευ ψυχῆς οὐ ζῇ ταῦτα, ἀλλ' ἐκ τῶν συνουσῶν ψυχῶν ἔχει τὸ ζῆν. ὅμως καὶ ὁ Ἀβραὰμ τὸ ἄψυχον σῶμα νεκρὸν ὠνόμασεν. 1 Kor 15,30 Εἰ μὴ ἀθάνατος ἡ ψυχή, εἰ μὴ ἐγείρεται τὸ σῶμα, εἰ καὶ μάταιον τὸ κινδυνεύειν ὑπὲρ εὐσεβείας. 1 Kor 15,32 Ὅσον κατ' ἀνθρώπινον ἧκε λογισμόν, ἐθηριομάχησα ἐν Ἐφέσῳ ἐγὼ οὐκ ἂν ὑποστῆναι τοῦτο βουληθεὶς ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας, εἰ–νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται. 9 1 Kor 15,33 Μὴ πλανᾶσθε, ὦ Κορίνθιοι, ὡς μὴ ἐπιδιαμενούσης τῆς λογικῆς ψυχῆς· οἱ γὰρ ἀπατῶντες ὑμᾶς συμφθείρονται αὐτὴν φθείρεσθαι οἰόμενοι. ᾧ περίκειται σώματα, φασὶν ὅτι σπαταλητέον· αὔριον γὰρ ἀποθνήσκομεν, οὐκ οὔσης ἑτέρας ζωῆς παρὰ τὴν φαινομένην, ὡς τὰ ἄλογα ζῶα ὧν συναφανίζεται ἡ ψυχὴ τῷ σώματι, ἐπειδὴ καὶ συνεσπάρη αὐτῷ. οὐκ ἀνεκτέον οὖν τῶν φαύλων διαλέξεων φθειρουσῶν εὐήθων τὰς γνώμας. 1 Kor 15,34 Γρηγορητέον κατὰ τὴν νόησιν ἵνα μὴ ἁμαρτάνειν συμβῇ ἐν τῷ συγκατατίθεσθαι τῇ σαθρᾷ περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἀπάτῃ. καλῶς δὲ καὶ τὸ ἐκνήψατε δικαίως ὡς μὴ πάντων τοῦτο ποιούντων· οἱ γὰρ σοφοὶ τοῦ κακοποιῆσαι ἀγρυπνοῦντες περὶ τὰ βλαβερὰ ἀδίκως ἐκνήφουσιν ἀποβαλόντες δῆθεν τὸν τῆς ἀμαθίας ὕπνον. 1 Kor 15,35-40 Ὁ ἐν Χριστῷ λαλῶν τῷ ἀμφιβάλλοντι περὶ τῆς τῶν νεκρῶν ἀναστάσεως ὡς ἀσυνέτως φησίν· ἄφρων, εἰ ἀμφιβάλλεις ὅτι τὸ νεκρωθὲν ἀνθρώπου σῶμα ἐγείρεται, ἴσθι ὅτι ἃ σπείρεις σπέρματα ἀποθανόντα εἰς τὴν γὴν καταβάλλεις πεπεισμένος ὡς οὐκ ἂν μεταβάλλοι εἰς φυτά, εἰ μὴ νεκρωθέντα σπαρείη. Ἕτερόν ἐστι τὸ ἐγειρόμενον σῶμα παρ' ὃ ἔσπειρας· σὺ μὲν γὰρ κόκκον ἔβαλες εἰς τὴν γήν, ὁ δὲ θεὸς στάχυν ἤγειρεν. πρὸς μίαν δὲ τῶν ἐρωτήσεων τὴν λέγουσαν πῶς ἐγείρονται νεκροί, ὁ περὶ τῶν σπειρομένων λόγος· πρὸς δὲ τὸ ἕτερον ἐρώτημα, τὸ ποίῳ δὲ σώματι ἔρχονται, ἐκ διαιρέσεως ἀποδίδωσι τὴν ἀπόδειξιν, καὶ διελὼν τὰ σώματα εἰς ἐπίγεια καὶ ἐπουράνια εἶπε κατὰ τὴν τῶν ἐπουρανίων ἡλίου καὶ σελήνης καὶ ἄστρων εἶναι τὴν τῶν ἐγειρομένων ἀνθρωπίνων σωμάτων δόξαν. 1 Kor 15,41 Ὅμοιοι τῇ τῶν φωστήρων καὶ ἀστέρων δόξῃ, οὐ πάντων τῶν ἀνισταμένων τὰ σώματα, ἀλλ' ἢ μόνον τῶν εὖ βεβιωκότων καὶ σωφρονισάντων· κἂν γὰρ τὰ τῶν φαύλων σώματα ἄφθαρτα ἐγείρονται, ἀλλ' οὖν στεροῦνται τῆς τῶν ἐπουρανίων δόξης. σημειωτέον δὲ ὅτι· ἡ δόξα τῶν ἐγειρομένων σωμάτων οὐσιώδης ἐστὶν ὡς καὶ ἡ τῶν φωστήρων. 10 1 Kor 15,42-43 Ὥσπερ ἡ λογικὴ ψυχὴ οὐκ οὖσα ἀρετὴ ἢ κακία δεκτικὴ ἀμφοτέρων ἐστὶ τούτων, οὕτω καὶ τὸ ἡμέτερον σῶμα οὐ φθορὰ ἢ ἀφθαρσία τυγχάνον δέχεται κατὰ διαφόρους χρόνους τὰς ἐγκειμένας οὐσιώδεις ποιότητας. 2 ἀμέλει γοῦν οὐ φθορὰ σπείρεται καὶ ἐγείρεται οὐκ ἀφθαρσία, ἀλλ' ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ. ἀκολουθεῖ δὲ τῷ ἐν φθορᾷ σπειρομένῳ τὸ ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ καὶ ἐν ἀτιμίᾳ καὶ σῶμα ψυχικὸν σπείρεσθαι, ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ τῷ ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ ἐγειρομένῳ τὸ ἐν δυνάμει καὶ δόξῃ καὶ σῶμα πνευματικὸν ἐγείρεσθαι.
thought_title: The kingdom handed over and the body's transformation
orientation: Didymus is commenting on 1 Corinthians 15:24-43, explaining how Christ hands over the kingdom to the Father, refuting heretics on baptism for the dead, and arguing that the risen body is not the same perishable body that was sown.
pass_a_gloss: He calls kingdom here the ones being ruled, that is his own flesh which the Son handed over to the Father after making it better, no longer being ruled as the form of a slave but as being flesh of the Word which is of the Son himself, having displayed the form of God in it. For then, when the Son has received back the glory which he had before the world existed, they will be ruled as by one king, Father and Son. Therefore Christ must reign for the advancement of all until all who are enemies because of sinning are placed under his feet, while he destroys every tyrannical authority, after which also the arch-evil one himself, death, is destroyed, since every soul united to him undergoes the death united to evil. They said these things were spoken against the mythology and deceit of the Greeks, of those who say that the gods are father-beaters, and that when the church is subjected he himself is said to be subjected, making his own the persecutions and sufferings and subjection of the church. The ones from Marcion baptize living people instead of unillumined dead people, not knowing that baptism saves only the one who has received it. But the apostle calls dead the bodies on behalf of which we are baptized; for by its own reason without soul these do not live, but from the souls present with them they have life. Nevertheless also Abraham named the soulless body dead. If the soul is not immortal, if the body is not raised, then also the risking for piety is vain. As far as according to human reasoning it comes, I fought with beasts in Ephesus, I would not have chosen to undergo this for the truth, if the dead are not raised. Do not be deceived, O Corinthians, as if the rational soul does not remain; for the ones deceiving you are corrupted together with it, thinking it is destroyed. To which bodies are attached, they say that one must live luxuriously; for tomorrow we die, there being no other life besides the visible one, as the irrational animals whose soul is destroyed together with the body, since it was also sown together with it. Therefore the worthless arguments corrupting the minds of the simple must not be tolerated. One must be watchful according to the mind so that it does not happen to sin in agreeing with the rotten deceit about the resurrection. And well also the 'sober up' justly, as not all do this; for the wise in doing evil, being sleepless about harmful things, sober up unjustly, having cast off supposedly the sleep of ignorance. The one speaking in Christ to the one doubting about the resurrection of the dead says as to a senseless one: fool, if you doubt that the dead body of a human is raised, know that the seeds which you sow you cast into the ground having died, being persuaded that they would not change into plants unless they were sown having died. The body being raised is different from what you sowed; for you threw a grain into the ground, but God raised up an ear of grain. To one of the questions, the one saying how are the dead raised, the word about the things being sown; to the other question, with what kind of body do they come, from division he gives the demonstration, and having divided bodies into earthly and heavenly he said that according to the glory of the heavenly sun and moon and stars is the glory of the raised human bodies. Similar to the glory of the luminaries and stars are the bodies not of all who are raised, but only of those who have lived well and been self-controlled; for even if the bodies of the wicked are raised incorruptible, nevertheless they are deprived of the glory of the heavenly ones. And it must be noted that: the glory of the raised bodies is substantial as also that of the luminaries. Just as the rational soul, not being virtue or vice, is receptive of both of these, so also our body, not being corruption or incorruptibility, receives according to different times the substantial qualities placed in it. Certainly then it is not sown corruption and raised not incorruptibility, but in incorruptibility. And it follows for the one sown in corruption to be sown in weakness and in dishonor and as a natural body, and likewise for the one raised in incorruptibility to be raised in power and glory and as a spiritual body.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the present passive participle, preserving the verbal force of being under rule rather than a noun like 'subjects'.
Compound adjective rendered literally to preserve the prefix ἀρχι- indicating primacy in evil, matching Didymus's personification of death.
Literal rendering of the alpha-privative adjective, preserving the baptismal imagery of illumination that Didymus contrasts with Marcionite practice.
Verbal adjective rendered with impersonal necessity to preserve the force of the -τέον ending, matching the heretics' slogan.
Compound verb rendered literally to preserve the συν- prefix indicating joint destruction of soul with body, which Didymus attributes to the heretics' view of irrational animals.
Literal rendering of the aorist imperative, preserving the metaphor of waking from drunkenness or stupor that Paul uses and Didymus comments on.

pass_b_english: Here Paul calls the kingdom the ones being ruled—that is, his own flesh, which the Son handed over to the Father after making it better, no longer being ruled in the form of a servant but as being the flesh of the Word, which is the Son himself, having displayed the form of God in it. For then, when the Son has received back the glory he had before the world existed, they will be ruled by one king, the Father and the Son. Christ must therefore reign for the advancement of all, until all who are enemies because of sinning are placed under his feet, while he destroys every tyrannical authority. After that, death itself, the arch-evil one, is also destroyed, since every soul united to it undergoes death, which is united to wickedness.

Some commentators say these words were spoken against Greek mythology and deception—against those who claim the gods are father-killers—and that when the church is subjected, he himself is said to be subjected, appropriating to himself the persecutions, the sufferings, and the subjection of the church.

The Marcionites baptize living people on behalf of unillumined dead people, not knowing that baptism saves only the one who receives it. But the apostle calls our bodies dead, on whose behalf we are baptized; for by their own nature, without a soul, these do not live, but they have life from the souls that are present with them. Likewise Abraham also called the soulless body dead.
If the soul is not immortal, if the body is not raised, then risking danger for the sake of piety is futile.
As far as human reasoning goes, Paul says, "I fought with wild beasts in Ephesus; I would not have endured this for the truth, if the dead are not raised."

Do not be deceived, Corinthians, as though the rational soul does not endure. For those who deceive you corrupt others along with themselves, thinking that it is destroyed. Since bodies are wrapped around it, they say one must live luxuriously: for tomorrow we die, since there is no other life besides the visible one, as with irrational animals whose soul is destroyed together with the body, because it was sown together with it. So the worthless arguments that corrupt the minds of the simple must not be tolerated.

We must keep watch in our understanding, so that we do not happen to sin by consenting to the rotten deception about the resurrection. And "sober up" is well said—rightly so—since not all do this. For those who are clever at doing evil stay awake over harmful things and sober up for wicked ends, supposedly casting off the sleep of ignorance.

Paul, speaking in Christ, says to the one doubting about the resurrection of the dead, as to one who is unintelligent: Fool, if you doubt that the dead body of a human being is raised, know that the seeds you sow you cast into the ground dead, convinced that they would not change into plants unless sown dead. The body that is raised is different from the one you sowed: you cast a grain into the ground, but God raised up an ear of wheat. The argument about seeds answers one of the questions—the one that says, how are the dead raised? To the other question, with what kind of body do they come, he gives the proof by division, and dividing bodies into earthly and heavenly, he said that the glory of the raised human bodies is according to that of the heavenly sun, moon, and stars.

Like the glory of the lights and stars are not the bodies of all who are raised, but only those of the ones who have lived well and been self-controlled. For even if the bodies of the wicked are raised incorruptible, they are nevertheless deprived of the glory of the heavenly bodies. And it must be noted that the glory of the raised bodies is essential, just as is that of the lights.

Just as the rational soul, not being virtue or vice, is receptive of both of these, so also our body, not being corruption or incorruptibility, receives at different times the essential qualities that are placed in it. At any rate, it is not sown as corruption, nor is it raised as incorruptibility, but it is raised in incorruptibility. To what is sown in corruption follows being sown in weakness and dishonor and as a natural body; likewise, what is raised in incorruptibility corresponds to what is raised in power and glory and as a spiritual body.

problems.quote: for those who deceive you are themselves corrupted along with it
problems.source_quote: οἱ γὰρ ἀπατῶντες ὑμᾶς συμφθείρονται αὐτὴν φθείρεσθαι οἰόμενοι
problems.why: The source does not say the deceivers are themselves corrupted; this clause is added.
problems.fix: for those who deceive you think the soul is being destroyed

problems.why: Source infinitive is purpose: 'to improve it'. English reads as completed action.
problems.fix: which the Son handed over to the Father to make it better
problems.ruling: βελτιῶσαι = aorist infinitive purpose ‘to improve’, not completed action ‘after making it better’.

problems.quote: since every soul united to him undergoes the death that is united to wickedness
problems.source_quote: ἐπείπερ πᾶσα ἑνουμένη αὐτῷ ψυχὴ ὑφισταμένη θάνατον τὸν ἑνούμενον τῇ κακίᾳ
problems.why: 'αὐτῷ' refers to the arch-evil one/death, not Christ; 'ὑφισταμένη' means 'subsisting', not 'undergoes'.
problems.fix: since every soul united to it subsists in the death that is united to wickedness
problems.ruling: αὐτῷ refers to death (arch‑evil one), not Christ; ὑφισταμένη = ‘subsisting’, not ‘undergoes’.

problems.quote: They say these things were said against the mythology and deceit of the Greeks

problems.quote: making his own the persecutions, sufferings, and subjection of the church.
problems.source_quote: οἰκειούμενος τῆς ἐκκλησίας τοὺς διωγμοὺς καὶ τὰ πάθη καὶ τὴν ὑποταγήν.
problems.why: Greek says Christ is analogous to the church’s persecutions, not that he causes them.
problems.fix: being analogous to the church’s persecutions, sufferings, and subjection.

problems.quote: Since bodies surround it, they say one must live luxuriously:
problems.source_quote: ᾧ περίκειται σώματα, φασὶν ὅτι σπαταλητέον· αὔριον γὰρ ἀποθνήσκομεν, οὐκ οὔσης ἑτέρας ζωῆς παρὰ τὴν φαινομένην, ...
problems.why: Greek says bodies are “σπαταλητέον” (to be wasted), not that one must live luxuriously; the added “Since bodies surround it” is also absent.
problems.fix: Since bodies are considered waste, they say we should not waste them...

edits.old: making his own the persecutions, sufferings, and subjection of the church.
edits.new: being analogous to the church’s persecutions, sufferings, and subjection.

edits.old: Since bodies surround it, they say one must live luxuriously:
edits.new: Since bodies are considered waste, they say one must live luxuriously:

fixed: Agency: 'οἰκειούμενος' means 'making one's own' or 'appropriating,' but in context it means Christ identifies with the church's experiences, not that he causes them. The English 'making his own' could be read as causative; 'being analogous to' better captures the sense of identification.

Mistranslation: 'ᾧ περίκειται σώματα' means 'to which bodies are attached' or 'which is surrounded by bodies,' referring to the soul. The Greek 'σπαταλητέον' is a verbal adjective meaning 'to be lived luxuriously' or 'to be indulged,' not 'to be wasted.' The English 'Since bodies surround it' is a mistranslation of the relative clause; the subject is the soul, and the phrase means 'since bodies are attached to it [the soul].' The suggested fix 'Since bodies are considered waste' is incorrect; the correct rendering is 'Since bodies are attached to it, they say one must live luxuriously.'

problems.quote: they say one must live luxuriously
problems.why: Greek means ‘to be wasted/spent’, not ‘to live luxuriously’; adds opposite connotation.

problems.quote: being analogous to the church's persecutions, sufferings, and subjection

problems.why: οἰκειούμενος means 'appropriating' or 'claiming as his own,' not 'being analogous to.' Christ claims the church's sufferings as his own.
problems.fix: claiming as his own the church's persecutions, sufferings, and subjection
problems.ruling: οἰκειούμενος = appropriating/claiming as his own; "analogous" loses sense of Christ taking on the church's sufferings

fixed: The English 'to improve it' misstates the source βελτιῶσαι, which is an aorist participle meaning 'after making it better'; restored 'after making it better'.
The source has no explicit subject for the saying; 'Some commentators' is a reasonable clarification for the unidentified speakers, and the English is otherwise accurate.
The source has a conditional structure (εἰ μὴ... εἰ μὴ... εἰ καὶ μάταιον); the English lacked the main clause 'then', so added it.
The source ἀδίκως ἐκνήφουσιν means 'sober up unjustly' but the English 'sober up unjustly' is awkward; 'for wicked ends' better conveys the sense of unjustly staying awake for harmful purposes.

The source νεκροὺς λέγει τὰ σώματα ὑπὲρ ὧν βαπτιζόμεθα means 'calls the bodies dead on behalf of which we are baptized'; the English was a word-for-word gloss that was confusing, so rephrased to 'calls our bodies dead, on whose behalf we are baptized'.
The source has Paul speaking in the first person (ἐθηριομάχησα ἐν Ἐφέσῳ ἐγὼ); the English did not mark this as Paul's words, so added 'Paul says' with quotation marks.
The source ὁ ἐν Χριστῷ λαλῶν means 'the one speaking in Christ', which is Paul; the English circumlocution was unclear, so clarified as 'Paul, speaking in Christ'.

previous_english: Here Paul calls the kingdom the ones being ruled—that is, his own flesh, which the Son handed over to the Father to make it better, no longer being ruled as the form of a slave but as being the flesh of the Word, which is the Son himself, having displayed the form of God in it. For then, when the Son has received back the glory he had before the world existed, they will be ruled as by one king, Father and Son. So Christ must reign for the advancement of all until all who are enemies because of sinning are placed under his feet, as he destroys every tyrannical authority, after which the arch-evil one himself, death, is also destroyed, since every soul united to it subsists in the death that is united to wickedness.

Those who claim the gods are father-beaters say these things were said against the mythology and deceit of the Greeks, and that when the church is subjected, he himself is said to be subjected, claiming as his own the church’s persecutions, sufferings, and subjection.

The Marcionites baptize living people on behalf of the dead who were unillumined, not knowing that baptism saves only the one who receives it. But the apostle calls the bodies dead on behalf of which we are baptized; for by their own nature, without a soul, these do not live, but they have life from the souls that are present with them. Likewise Abraham also called the soulless body dead.
If the soul is not immortal, if the body is not raised, then even the danger undertaken for piety is vain.
As far as human reasoning goes, I fought with beasts in Ephesus, and I would not have chosen to endure this for the truth if the dead are not raised.

Do not be deceived, Corinthians, as though the rational soul does not endure; for those who deceive you think the soul is being destroyed. Since bodies are considered waste, they say it is wasteful: for tomorrow we die, there being no other life besides the visible one, as with irrational animals whose soul is destroyed together with the body, since it was sown together with it. So the worthless arguments that corrupt the minds of the simple must not be tolerated.

We must keep watch in our understanding so that we do not happen to sin by agreeing with the rotten deceit about the resurrection. And the phrase "sober up righteously" is well said, since not all do this; for those who are wise at doing evil keep awake over harmful things and sober up unrighteously, supposedly casting off the sleep of ignorance.

The one speaking in Christ says to the one doubting about the resurrection of the dead, as to a fool: Fool, if you doubt that the dead body of a human being is raised, know that the seeds you sow you cast into the ground after they have died, convinced that they would not change into plants unless they were sown after dying. The body that is raised is different from what you sowed; for you cast a grain into the ground, but God raised up an ear of wheat. The argument about the things sown answers one of the questions, the one that says, "How are the dead raised?" To the other question, "With what kind of body do they come?" he gives the demonstration by division, and dividing bodies into earthly and heavenly, he said that the glory of the raised human bodies is according to that of the heavenly bodies—sun, moon, and stars.

The bodies of all who are raised are not like the glory of the luminaries and stars, but only those of the ones who have lived well and been disciplined; for even if the bodies of the wicked are raised incorruptible, they are nevertheless deprived of the glory of the heavenly bodies. And it must be noted that the glory of the raised bodies is essential, just as is that of the luminaries.

Just as the rational soul, not being virtue or vice, is receptive of both of these, so also our body, not being corruption or incorruptibility, receives at different times the essential qualities that are placed in it. At any rate, it is not corruption that is sown and not incorruptibility that is raised, but it is raised in incorruptibility. And what follows for what is sown in corruption is that it is sown in weakness and dishonor and as a natural body; likewise, what follows for what is raised in incorruptibility is that it is raised in power and glory and as a spiritual body.
